Redoubtable

/rih-DOW-tuh-buhl/ - the stress falls on DOW · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Redoubtable means formidable; commanding fear and respect.

Entries in the pie division doubled the summer the county fair's redoubtable head judge finally retired.

Worked Example

Forgers keep a list, and Osei Mensah's name sits at the top of it. In thirty years of vetting paintings he has unmasked four hundred fakes and never once cleared one; dealers hoping to slip something past a sale quietly withdraw the lot when they hear he will inspect it. He is redoubtable — feared the way only the truly respected are feared.

Redoubtable braids two feelings that usually travel separately: dread and admiration. A fearsome foe scares you; an admired one earns your salute; the redoubtable one does both at once — you dread the contest precisely because you know how good they are. The word is praise wearing armor.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

fearsome: feared, full stop — the respect is optional

imposing: impressive enough to daunt at first sight, before any contest begins

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

harmless: no threat to anyone

meek: gentle and timid, stirring no fear in anyone

Where it sits · how much dread the opponent inspires — competent → redoubtable → invincible

competent vs. redoubtable: Competent does the job well and earns a nod; redoubtable earns something closer to a gulp.

invincible vs. redoubtable: Invincible goes past redoubtable: the redoubtable titleholder is dreaded but can be beaten on a great day; the invincible one, by definition, cannot.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: thoroughly (an intensifier)

Root — doubt

Root — doubt: to fear (Old French douter, which meant both 'to doubt' and 'to fear')

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: worthy to be

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (thoroughly) + doubt (to fear, from Old French douter) + -able (worthy to be) = thoroughly to be feared. Douter once meant fear as well as uncertainty, and redoubtable preserves that lost sense in amber. Even the silent b is a family trait: scribes slipped it into both doubt and redoubtable to show off the Latin ancestor dubitare.

Use the root in a new word: doubt

Use the root in a new word: doubt: To doubt a story is to hold back from it — douter once meant to fear it too, and redoubtable keeps the fear.

Word Choice

formal / admiring, slightly antique

Redoubtable is praise wearing armor: the foe everyone dreads because everyone respects them. It keeps a faint period costume — redoubtable aunts, litigators, examiners — and it braids fear with admiration. Fearsome alone scares; redoubtable also salutes.
